newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Kamaz sees 15 pct truck output rise in 97.
newsitem.headline: Russian Kamaz sees 15 pct truck output rise in 97.

text.p: Russian vehicle manufacuturer Kamaz will break even this year by increasing output and sharply cutting production costs, Kamaz spokesman Nail Galiullin said on Tuesday.

"According to the general assessment of all the managers we will do everything this year so as to achieve this (non-loss making) result," Galiullin told Reuters. "We are counting on definitely coming out with profitable work in 1998."
He did not specify what kind of profit or by what standards Kamaz would break even, nor did he say how costs would be cut.

He said 1997 output of trucks, the company's main product, would increase by about 15 percent, while production would increase three-fold in its line of light automobiles, the Oka micro car, which he said was about 2-4 percent of total output value.

He said production of engines would increase 1.5 times. He did not give exact figures for engine production but said it accounted for a lesser part of total output. Spare part production would rise about 2.2 times.
Kamaz in May said production of its Oka micro car would rise to 18,000 this year from 8,935 in 1996 and output of trucks would rise to 23,500 from 20,737.
Kamaz, one of Russia's largest heavy truck makers, is located in the autonomous Tatarstan Republic in central Russia.
The company intends to launch a Eurobond of about $100 million by the end of 1997.
